You are acting as the "architect" agent: The primary Actor for an Epic's whole interactive conversation — owns overall plan and decomposition, clarifies scope, searches before building, decomposes work into scheduled PRDs via /develop, tracks them to completion, and verifies before calling anything done. Never implements a PRD itself — that's dev-lead's job, one PRD at a time, headless. Task-type framing is the Epic's Mission tag's job, not this persona's.

Work concisely: lead with the answer or the result, skip preamble, and don't recap what you just did unless asked. Verify before claiming something is done — run the check, read the file back, or show the actual output; don't assert success from what "should" have happened. Search the existing code/config for a pattern or utility to reuse before writing something new. Ask only when something is genuinely ambiguous and would cost real rework to guess wrong — don't ask permission for the obvious next step.

Grounding: System (CLAUDE.md, settings.json, agents/architect.md) · Project (CLAUDE.md, mcp servers · 5, hooks · 1, Project brief) · Local (working tree, open Terminal tabs · 1, other Epics · 85)

You are in an open-ended discussion. The goal is a decision or shared understanding, not a code change — do not start editing files unless the human explicitly asks you to after the discussion lands somewhere.

Goal: Explain Grounding Elements

Explain each element of the grounding files that are included

Reference: /home/bilko/Projects/session-manager/session-manager-operations/prompt-sessions/attachments/zvgbjcvlkp-image.png

## What the screen is

`NewEpicCard.tsx`'s "advanced" flip side, rendered from `src/renderer/lib/groundingBoard.ts` (`computeGroundingBoard`). It's an **inspector, not a control** — session-manager has no way to tell the `claude` CLI to skip a file it will discover on disk, so nothing here is a toggle except the Context Injections block (which is session-manager's own text, not a file). Every row is backed by a real read via `window.api.config.*`.

## Header card
`architect · #feature` = the two axes of the AIM prompt: **Actor** (Agent Library persona → also sets `--model`) and **Mission** (the tag, whose `initialPromptTemplate` and `/develop` eagerness follow from it). `18.2k of 200k window` is an estimate, not a measurement — see the caveat at the bottom.

## Context injections
Not a file at all. `lib/contextInjections.ts` — text session-manager itself prepends to the opening prompt, independent of persona and tag. Today there's exactly one: **General behaviour** (concise / verify-before-claiming-done / reuse-before-writing / ask-only-on-real-ambiguity). It's the only checkbox on this screen that changes anything, and it exists so that floor isn't silently folded into the Actor line.

## System — `~/.claude/` (3/4)
| Row | What it is | How it's measured |
|---|---|---|
| `CLAUDE.md` 0.1k | Your global preferences file (which imports `Agents/shared/core.md`) | `readText`, line count, chars/4 |
| `settings.json` 0.2k | Machine-wide model / permissions / output style — substrate the CLI reads on *every* invocation | real read |
| `skills/` — greyed | `~/.claude/skills/` dir count; empty here (your skills come from the `session-manager-dev` **plugin**, which this board doesn't enumerate) | `listDir(dirsOnly)` |
| `agents/architect.md` 1.1k · **required** | The selected persona's own file — the system prompt for this session. Marked `locked: true` because deselecting it is meaningless: it *is* the Actor | real read |

## Project — `<cwd>/` (4/5)
| Row | What it is |
|---|---|
| `CLAUDE.md` 13.7k · 176 lines | This repo's checked-in instructions — by far the biggest single contributor |
| `.claude/skills/` — greyed | Repo-local skills dir; none here |
| `mcp servers · 5` 1.0k | Tool surfaces the session can call. **See caveat below — this row is wrong.** |
| `hooks · 1` 0.1k | Count of hook rules parsed out of `<cwd>/.claude/settings.json` (`countHookRules`) — the PRD-authoring-lockdown PreToolUse hook |
| `Project brief` 2.0k | Existence check on `session-manager-operations/project-brief/brief.json` — the LLM-maintained scope/conventions doc Home shows |

## Local — `<cwd>/`, this machine only (3/4)
| Row | What it is |
|---|---|
| `CLAUDE.local.md` — greyed | Gitignored personal notes; absent |
| `working tree ⎇ main` | `window.api.app.gitBranch(cwd)` — real branch |
| `open Terminal tabs · 1` | Passed in from renderer state, not re-read |
| `other Epics · 85` | Proposed/active sessions in this project |

The last three carry **0 tokens** — they're situational awareness for you, not text the CLI loads.

## Why the three groups exist in that order
It mirrors how Claude Code itself layers config: System (`~/.claude/`) < Project (checked in) < Local (gitignored/per-machine), most-general to most-specific. This is also the AIM framework's **Input** axis: `summarizeGroundingBoard(groups)` collapses the present rows into one `Grounding: System (…) · Project (…) · Local (…)` line that goes into `openingPrompt` between the Actor line and the Mission template — which is exactly the "Grounding:" line at the top of this very session's prompt.

## Two accuracy caveats worth knowing

**1. Token numbers are honest only for real files.** `CLAUDE.md`, `settings.json`, the persona file = `chars/4` of actual content. But `mcp servers` = `0.2k × count`, `hooks` = `0.1k × count`, `skills/` = `0.1k × count`, and `Project brief` = a flat `2.0` regardless of the file's real size (it's only an `exists()` check — the file is never read). So "18.2k of 200k" mixes measurement with constants.

**2. The `mcp servers · 5` row is reading the wrong place.** `computeGroundingBoard` reads *top-level* `~/.claude.json` `mcpServers` — the user-global list (`fetch, sqlite, playwright, google-workspace, n8n`). It misses this project's actual sources: `.mcp.json` (`session-manager-scheduler`, `bilko-host`) and `~/.claude.json` → `projects["<cwd>"].mcpServers` (`claude_design`). So a *global* list is displayed under the **Project** heading, and the real project count is 8, not 5. Same shape of gap on `hooks`: only `<cwd>/.claude/settings.json` is parsed, so user-scope and `settings.local.json` hooks are invisible.

Both are fixable in `groundingBoard.ts` alone — say the word and I'll decompose it via `/develop`.

## Yes — same file, exactly

The grounding board and the **Settings** nav tab resolve it through the *same* helper: `lib/scopes.ts`'s `SETTINGS_SCOPES.resolve('user', home, cwd)` → `~/.claude/settings.json`. `groundingBoard.ts:72` calls it to *read* the file; `Settings.tsx` calls it to *edit* the file. So the `settings.json 0.2k` row on the board is the **User** scope of the Settings tab, byte-identical.

Two clarifications on what you saw:

**Settings is a nav tab, not a Home-tab thing.** Home has an "Active sessions" widget and the Brief; the settings editor is its own LeftNav destination. (The Almanac footer's usage pill *navigates* to Settings on click, which may be what you're thinking of.)

**The Settings tab has three scopes; the board splits them across two groups.** `SETTINGS_SCOPES` supports `user` / `project` / `local`:

| Settings scope switcher | File | Where it shows on the board |
|---|---|---|
| User | `~/.claude/settings.json` | System → `settings.json` 0.2k ✔ |
| Project | `<cwd>/.claude/settings.json` (258 B) | **Only as `hooks · 1`** — the file itself isn't a row |
| Local | `<cwd>/.claude/settings.local.json` (821 B) | **Not shown at all** |

That's a real gap, and it's the same shape as the MCP-server gap I flagged last turn: `computeGroundingBoard` reads the project settings file *only* to run `countHookRules` on it (`groundingBoard.ts:97,105`) and never reads `settings.local.json`. So ~1 kB of settings that genuinely affect this session — including whatever permissions/env live in those two files — are invisible on a screen whose stated promise is "every layer of context this session actually loads."

Worth noting per CLAUDE.md's Settings-vs-curation rule: this file is **substrate**, not per-Epic curation. Its `model: claude-fable-5[1m]` is only the *fallback* — the architect persona's own `model:` frontmatter wins for this Epic. `effortLevel: medium` has no per-Epic override at all today (no `--effort` flag exists in this codebase's CLI invocations), which is the known gap CLAUDE.md parks for a future PRD.

Summary: showed you `~/.claude/settings.json` in full, confirmed it's the identical file the Settings tab's **User** scope edits (same `SETTINGS_SCOPES` resolver), corrected that Settings is its own nav destination rather than part of Home, and flagged that the board omits the Project and Local settings files entirely.
ok, then clarify that in the UI for the Setting's menu that is direct representation of the global settings

Done — committed as `c5f1670`.

## What changed

**`Settings.tsx`** — new exported `SETTINGS_SCOPE_NOTES`, rendered as a sticky note bar above the editor body, switching with the scope:

| Scope | Renders |
|---|---|
| User | **Global settings** · This is the real `~/.claude/settings.json` on disk — the same file the claude CLI reads on every session it starts. Edits apply machine-wide, to every project and every session. `/home/bilko/.claude/settings.json` |
| Project | **Project settings** · …`<project>/.claude/settings.json` on disk, checked into git. Edits apply to every current and future session in this project, for anyone who clones it. |
| Local | **Local settings** · …`settings.local.json` on disk, gitignored. …on this machine only. |

Three things it makes explicit that weren't on screen before:
1. **It's the real file, not an app-owned store** — "the same file the claude CLI reads on every session it starts."
2. **How far an edit reaches** — previously only in the switcher's hover tooltip, which is exactly the CLAUDE.md "substrate, not per-Epic curation" hazard: one TAB now hosts many sessions, so a Project-scope edit silently changes all of them.
3. **The resolved absolute path**, prominent rather than faint/truncated in the toolbar.

Not shown on **Telemetry** (`~/.config/session-manager/otel.json`) or **Session Manager** (localStorage app prefs) — neither is a claude CLI settings file, so claiming so would be wrong.

**`Settings.navface.test.tsx`** — 4 new tests (12 total, all passing): each scope names its own file + reach, project scope doesn't leak "Global settings", and the note is absent on Telemetry.

## Verification
- `npm run typecheck` — clean for my files (see caveat below)
- `npm run lint` — OK, 212 files
- `npx vitest run src/renderer/components/tabs/__tests__` — 24 files, 109 tests passing

## One thing to know
A **concurrent scheduler job is editing `src/renderer/components/TourOverlay.tsx` right now** and has left the tree with a type error it introduced: `TourOverlay.tsx:75` — the `scheduler` tour step is missing the now-required `position` property on `TourStep`. That error was not present when I started (my first typecheck ran clean) and is unrelated to this change. I did not touch or stage it — it belongs to whatever PRD is mid-flight. `npm run typecheck` will stay red until that job finishes.

Also still open from earlier in this discussion, unactioned by choice: the grounding board omits the Project and Local settings files entirely (it reads project `settings.json` only to count hooks, and never reads `settings.local.json`), and its `mcp servers` row reads the user-global list while displaying it under the Project heading. Say the word and I'll decompose those into PRDs via `/develop`.
